Commentary.Commentary: The umpire have made their way into the ground followed by the players of Bangladesh. Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Ibrahim Zadran are the two openers for Afghanistan. Hasan Mahmud will start the proceedings for Bangladesh with the ball in his hands. The revised target under the DLS method would be 164 in 43 overs.
...RUN CHASE...

The visitors were brilliant with the ball and ripped through the batting lineup of Bangladesh. Fazalhaq Farooqi was brilliant at the top as he kept the scoring rate down at the top and forced the batters to play false strokes for their dismissals, he ended up with 3 scalps under his name but did go off the field with a niggle in the final over. Mujeeb Ur Rahman and Rashid Khan took a couple of wickets each while they were well helped by Mohammad Nabi who took a solo wicket but an important one of Najmul Hossain Shanto. The score is not a big one but the overcast conditions and the ting of grass on the field will surely help the bowlers. Let's see who comes out on top in the second half of the game. Join us for the chase at 7.20 pm IST (1.50 pm GMT).

In a rain-curtailed game, Afghanistan would be happy to walk get back into the dugout after restricting the hosts for a below par-total. We are at the halfway stage of the game with Afghanistan restricting Bangladesh to a total of 169. The game started with a flurry of runs but wickets at regular intervals held the run rate and put the hosts on the back foot in this game. After being asked to bat first Tamim Iqbal started watchfully but edged one in the hands of Rahmanullah Gurbaz and that opened the flood gates which led to the fall of wickets on a frequent basis. The top four got in but failed to score big while Towhid Hridoy was the only one who batted deep and scored 51 valuable runs being the top scorer of the team.

A single to finish and just two runs come off the final over. Fullish length again outside off, sliced away by Mustafizur Rahman wide of the man at backward point. The fielder there dives to his left and makes a half stop. A single is taken and Bangladesh finish with 169/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin! The two umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Afghanistan. We can also see Mohammad Saleem being presented with the cap as he is set to make his ODI debut. Tamim Iqbal and Litton Das are the openers for Bangladesh.It will be Fazalhaq Farooqi to open the proceedings with the ball here. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Atar Ali Khan is pitchside. He says that a lot of grass has been left on the pitch and it will provide help to the seamers and back of the length delivery will be key here as the ball will do a lot of lateral movement from there.

Bangladesh skipper, Tamim Iqbal says that they are happy to bat here and it may well quicken up later in the day. Adds that the intent will be to stay positive but sometimes they play the situation too. Mentions that the key will be to negotiate the first 10 over well without any scoreboard pressure. Informs that the preparation for this game has been very well now it is time to execute the plans.

Hashmatullah Shahidi, the captain of Afghanistan says they would like to field first as it looks like the pitch has a bit of moisture and they want to take advantage of it for the first 10-15 overs. Adds that the team is well prepared for the conditions here. Mentions that Rashid Khan is in the side and that's a big boost for them all and they will be looking to restrict them under 250.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Mohammad Nabi, Najibullah Zadran, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Azmatullah Omarzai, and Mohammad Saleem (On debut).

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tamim Iqbal (C), Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Towhid Hridoy, Shakib Al Hasan, Mushfiqur Rahim (WK), Afif Hossain, Mehidy Hasan, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, and Hasan Mahmud.
TOSS - Afghanistan have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

Afghanistan on the contrary are a hot and cold side as when the batting clicks they do well but if it fails it does fail miserably. The team is heavily dependent on players like Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Hashmatullah Shahidi, and Ibrahim Zadran for the batting department while the bowling rests on the shoulders of Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman and veteran Mohammad Nabi. The battle between the spinners of Afghanistan and the batters of Bangladesh would be one to keep a keen eye on. Let's see who draws the first blood in the battle between the giant killers as Afghanistan takes on Bangladesh. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

The hosts Bangladesh are in wonderland as they have defeated the likes of India, England, and Ireland in the last three ODI series they have played at home. The bowling has been a revolution for the Asian giant killers and players like Taskin Ahmed, Ebadot Hossain and Hasan Mahmud have bowled in a splendid manner recently. The batting has been solid too as Najmul Hossain Shanto, Litton Das and Mushfiqur Rahim have stood-up big time for the side. The team would be heavily dependent on the bowling attack as they have run riots against every opponent they have faced in recent times.
